results.title: Broad roller floor and return backing construction packaging piece flow transfer

synopsis.reason: Identified function and exact source snapshot retained.

construction.value: Ten inclined rollers drive fuel toward a four-motor feeder. A low-friction backing panel redirects loose inventory toward the entry. The team later combined feeder and floor powertrains.
construction.reason: Selected contacts and drives explained; no fabrication completeness claimed.

operating_sequence.value: A ball can arrive anywhere across the floor; successive rollers push it to the rising feeder. Balls hitting the front backing slide back toward the pickup region. During a pause the system must avoid packing fuel harder into an unavailable launcher.
operating_sequence.reason: Editorial sequence identifies a physical route; sensing/recovery and hidden transitions remain unresolved.

interfaces.value: Effective lane width, roller gaps, queue depth, compression distribution and reverse command order remain unresolved.
interfaces.reason: Physical dependency explained; not a dimensionally certified interface.

packaging.value: The rebuild uses a single front slapdown collector, an expanding storage enclosure over an inclined roller floor, and a full-width raised shooter at the opposite end. Corner swerve modules sit below this path; the launcher side structure carries the drum and hood and attaches down toward the drive rails. Source dimensions give a 27.5 by 27-inch frame. The hopper panels and their joints surround the ball path, so screw heads on the hood can rub a sliding wall. A source reply specifically explains using flathead screws there. Some electronics moved above the brainpan, but under-pan equipment still needs underside access. Preserve that service split. Do not infer battery removal without its source view.

The inspected CAD screenshot shows wide transverse rollers and launcher motors packed into the central space between modules. The launcher changes elevation instead of yawing independently of the chassis. Its feed transmission is organized around the elevation pivot so a ring can pass into the launcher across its angle range. A raised climb/trap pose shown in another source image is not the everyday driving envelope. Battery location and removal path cannot be established from these images, and are deliberately omitted from the layout.
